evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 131: cum sōlus rem pūblicam regeret (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Sen. 37: tantam domum … Appius regēbat
terms.comment: Of a state, a household, and oneself (animum rege, Hor. Ep. 1.2.62).

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, with the dative
evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.2.62–63: quī nisi pāret, imperat
terms.comment: To give orders and have them obeyed; the opposite is pārēre, obey.

evidence: Cic. Rep. 2.17: Rōmulus cum septem et trīgintā rēgnāvisset annōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a king’s rule, and of anyone who has his own way.

evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 131: orbemque terrārum gubernāret (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly to steer a ship (Greek κυβερνάω); a favourite figure of Cicero’s for governing (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: īra furor brevis est; animum rege, quī nisi pāret, imperat
phrases.english: anger is a short madness; rule your temper, for if it does not obey, it commands

phrases.latin: Rēgnat, nōn regitur, quī nīl nisi quod vult facit.
phrases.english: whoever does nothing but what he wants is the ruler, not the ruled

phrases.latin: quattuor rōbustōs fīliōs, quīnque fīliās, tantam domum, tantās clientēlās Appius regēbat et caecus et senex
phrases.english: four strong sons, five daughters, so great a household, so many clients: Appius ruled them all, blind and old as he was
